platform.name: Identity Platform
platform.owner: Jane Smith, Director of Identity Engineering
platform.description: The enterprise platform providing authentication, authorisation, federation, and identity lifecycle services to all consuming applications.

boundary.inside: Authentication services, authorisation policy engine, federation gateway, identity lifecycle workflows, MFA service

platform.notes: Example: a partial population of the Identity Platform (P201) showing how the major entity types interrelate. Demonstrates ID conventions, structured narrative on Change, milestone roles, criterion-change relationships, transition between milestones, and external references. Industry-neutral by construction; capabilities are not anchored to any industry reference taxonomy (industry_reference_ids omitted) since identity capabilities are universal across industries. Organisations whose industry has an adopted reference taxonomy would populate industry_reference_ids on capabilities where it applies. Not a complete platform population; intended as a pattern guide.

capability.name: Authentication
capability.description: Verifying the identity of users and systems requesting access to enterprise resources.

capability.name: Federation
capability.description: Supporting federated authentication with external identity providers and downstream consumers.

component.name: Authentication Service (logical)
component.description: Logical authentication service providing federated identity verification with MFA. Technology-agnostic specification of what the platform requires.
component.notes: ABB-flavour Component: technology-agnostic logical description. This is what enterprise architecture would specify in Phase B/C before product selection.

component.name: Legacy LDAP authentication service
component.description: On-premise OpenLDAP-based authentication service supporting enterprise applications. End-of-life from vendor.
component.notes: SBB: the legacy concrete implementation (LDAP). Realises the same logical ABB but is technology-specific.

component.name: SSO Gateway (Okta on AWS)
component.description: Okta-based SSO gateway running on AWS, providing OAuth 2.1, OIDC, SAML 2.0, and MFA. Replaces the legacy LDAP service.
component.notes: SBB: the target concrete implementation (Okta-based). Realises the same logical ABB with modern technology.

driver.name: LDAP vendor end-of-life
driver.description: The LDAP vendor has announced end-of-life for the version we run, with security patch support ending in 18 months.

milestone.name: P201 Baseline
milestone.description: Current state of the Identity Platform at programme inception.

milestone.name: P201 M1: SSO Gateway operational
milestone.description: SSO Gateway operational for new applications; LDAP remains in service for legacy consumers.

milestone.name: P201 Target: LDAP retired, full federation operational

criterion.description: SSO Gateway is operational and certified for use by new applications.
Legacy LDAP service is decommissioned with no remaining consumers.

narrative.summary: Introduce a cloud-based SSO Gateway (Okta) to provide modern authentication and federation, initially for new applications.
narrative.rationale: LDAP cannot support modern federation protocols (OAuth 2.1, OIDC) now required by consuming applications and is end-of-life from the vendor. SSO Gateway addresses both the protocol gap and the EOL risk while enabling future federation.
narrative.outcome: SSO Gateway is operational in production, certified for enterprise applications, with MFA enabled by default and OAuth 2.1 / OIDC support fully functional.
narrative.target_effect: New Component introduced in 'active' lifecycle state, realising the Authentication and Federation capabilities of the Identity Platform.
narrative.constraints: Cannot be cut over to production traffic until certified by the security function and load-tested at 10x current LDAP peak.

narrative.summary: Retire the legacy LDAP authentication service after all consumers have migrated to the SSO Gateway.
narrative.rationale: LDAP is end-of-life from the vendor with security support ending. Retirement eliminates the concentration risk and unsupported-infrastructure risk currently carried.
narrative.outcome: LDAP service is decommissioned and removed from production. No application has a remaining dependency on LDAP. The component is marked retired in CMDB and LeanIX.
narrative.target_effect: Component lifecycle moves from 'deprecated' to 'retired'. The Authentication capability is no longer realised by LDAP.

commitment.committed_criteria_summary: SSO Gateway operational for new applications; MFA enabled; OAuth 2.1 support verified.

transition.health_basis: Initiative I-12 on track; SSO Gateway in UAT; no material slips declared.
Initiative I-14 (LDAP retirement) at risk: dependency on application teams completing migration is uncertain.

risk.name: Concentration of authentication on end-of-life LDAP infrastructure
risk.description: All enterprise authentication flows through LDAP. LDAP is end-of-life and unsupported within 18 months. Outage or security incident would affect all customer-facing services simultaneously.

standard.name: Authentication protocol standard
standard.description: All authentication services must support OAuth 2.1 or equivalent modern federation protocols. PKCE required for public clients. Refresh token rotation mandatory.
standard.waiver_process: Waiver Decision required from Architecture Review Board with security function endorsement.

interface.name: Enterprise SSO authentication contract
interface.notes: ABB-flavour Interface: the contract specification, published by enterprise architecture, reusable across implementations.

interface.name: SSO authentication endpoint (production)
interface.notes: SBB-flavour Interface: the specific endpoint at a particular URL, provided by a specific Component.
